text: California election offices can start opening and processing mail ballots up to 29 days before Election Day.

room.label: students (demo crowd)
room.note: No published poll has measured this belief yet. The 5C pilot survey replaces this split with real student answers.

truthSource.label: California Secretary of State: Vote Counting Process
truthSource.oneLine: County elections officials may begin opening and processing mail ballot envelopes up to 29 days before Election Day, but those results can’t be accessed or shared until all polls close.

lesson.tip: Opening envelopes and checking signatures early is legal and speeds up the count; releasing any results before polls close is not. When a post cries “they’re counting early,” ask whether anything was actually released.
